master_narrator.agency_handoff_prompt:
The table was silent. Not the good, tired silence of a job well done. The sharp, brittle silence of sixteen people who had been breathing the same recycled air for too long.

Hector was vibrating, tapping his spoon against the table. Silas was staring at a smudge on his glass. Kenna was trying to make eye contact with everyone, which Elias noted on his slate was only increasing the collective heart rate by four beats per minute. Mitigating Isolated-Confined-Extreme (ICE) Third-Quarter cortisol cascades and autonomic hypervigilance through structured communal roast rituals and oxytocin vagal buffering was his domain, yet right now, the theoretical models felt agonizingly inadequate.

"So," Dorian said beside Elias, his voice dry as parchment. "Who broke the water filtration system?"

Silence.

"It wasn't broken," Kaio mumbled. "It was... enhanced."

"Enhanced?" Ryn slammed a ladle down. "It was dispensing algae-sludge into the soup stock! I had to filter it through a sock, Kaio. A sock!"

"It was a clean sock!"

The table erupted. Arguments overlapped—engineering versus biology, safety versus discovery. Elias watched the textbook cascade of an isolated group under stress: the Third-Quarter Phenomenon, where morale bottoms out and sixteen polymaths channel days of radiation dread into a holy war over plumbing.

The noise washed over him. The instinct to intervene, to guide them toward a constructive resolution, was strong, but under the extreme stress of the escalating argument, Elias felt his Taurus override engage. He dug his heels in. He crossed his arms, his face setting into a mask of immovable, deadpan stubbornness. He would not stop them. He simply watched the chaos, refusing to move, silently demanding that they exhaust their own absurdity. He defended his own quiet space at the table, refusing to be drawn into the fray.

Then, Vex stood up.

"You're all ignoring the obvious," Vex declared, pointing at the ceiling. "Mercury is in retrograde. And Kaio is a Capricorn. It was inevitable."

The absurdity of the statement hung in the air. Silas blinked. "Mercury isn't even in this solar system, Vex."

"Spiritually, it is," Vex insisted.

A giggle snorted out of Zara. Then a chuckle from Leo. Suddenly, the tension broke. Elias lowered his slate as the laughter rolled across the timber hall—not polite laughter, but hysterical, rib-aching relief. The deliberate cognitive non-sequitur cleared the stress hormones faster than any logical intervention could have. They consumed the strange soup, their laughter mingling with the warmth of the hearth fire that attracted them all together.

"If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Elias noted with a dry, affectionate smile, his voice cutting through the noise.

"A sock," Ryn wiped a tear from her eye, handing a bowl to Elara, who was managing the triage of dinner service with her usual warm, commanding presence. "Kaio, you are banned from the plumbing. Forever."

"Accepted," Kaio grinned, reaching for the bread.

Elias uncrossed his arms, the stubborn weight in his chest lifting. The rust could wait. They were unbroken for one more night.
